description:
CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, invoked as the @Service it became rather than as a batch job: no EXEC PGM= names it anywhere under app/jcl, app/proc or app/csd, and all four of its call sites are online - CORPT00C :392 and :412, COTRN02C :393 and :413 - so it is a called subprogram whatever the mandated class name DateUtilityJob suggests, and it is reached through its typed method with no JobLauncher, no job repository and no HTTP layer in the path. LS-DATE='BC220719  ' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='<BC>YYMMDD' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (:84-:85), each written out to the full PIC X(10) width because the declared width changes the outcome - a longer mask would be truncated by the receiving PIC X(10) and would then report a different message entirely; LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (:86) is the whole output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. ParityCase has no member able to carry a CALL parameter - its inputs are seeded datasets, batch job parameters or an online screen request, and these two are none of the three - so the pair is restated here verbatim while CSUTLDTCParityTest.LINKAGE holds the authoritative copy; declaring them as jobParameters is refused outright, because only a BATCH_JOB may carry one and this program is reached by no JCL step. The program declares no ENVIRONMENT DIVISION, no SELECT and no FD - only WORKING-STORAGE at :22 and LINKAGE at :83 - so it seeds no dataset, writes no record, leaves no final state and takes no job parameter: its entire observable behaviour is the 80 bytes :97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity :98 moves into RETURN-CODE, which is 3 here and is deliberately not normalised to 4, 8 or 12. This is arm 5 of the ten-arm EVALUATE TRUE at :128, matched at :137 and moving 'Unsupp. Range  ' into WS-RESULT PIC X(15) at :138, with WHEN OTHER still last at :147; the arm order is itself the contract, because EVALUATE takes the first matching WHEN and a reordering would change which token selects which arm. That literal is author-padded - 'Unsupp. Range' is 13 characters and the source literal as written is 15 - so the abbreviation, its full stop and both in-literal trailing spaces are reproduced byte for byte rather than stripped and re-padded to a width. Severity 3 and message 2513 are DECODED from that arm's own 88-level VALUE X'000309D159C3C5C5' at :66: 0x0003 is the severity halfword, 0x09D1 is 9*256+209 = 2513, and the trailing C3 C5 C5 is the severity-control byte and the facility identifier 'CEE' in EBCDIC, which takes no part in the message. Neither number is interpolated from a neighbouring arm, because the nine are non-contiguous - the preceding arm is 2509 and this one skips 2510, 2511 and 2512 to reach 2513 - and it is emphatically not 2514, which no 88-level names at all. 2513 IS THE ONE ERROR VALUE BOTH ONLINE CALLERS DELIBERATELY ACCEPT, and that is why this single arm carries two of the twenty cases where most arms carry one. Each caller tests IF CSUTLDTC-RESULT-SEV-CD = '0000' first (COTRN02C :397, CORPT00C :396) and only then IF CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG-NUM NOT = '2513' (COTRN02C :400 and :420, CORPT00C :399 and :419), letting 2513 through silently and treating every other non-zero severity as 'Not a valid date...'. Both read those two spans through their own X(04) + X(11) + X(04) + X(61) breakdown of the same 80 bytes (COTRN02C :65-:69, CORPT00C :132-:136), which sums to 80 independently and corroborates severity at offset 0 and message number at offset 15. That tolerance is why WS-SEVERITY-N PIC 9(4) REDEFINES WS-SEVERITY PIC X(04) (:43-:44) must render the four-character string '0003' at offset 0 and WS-MSG-NO-N PIC 9(4) REDEFINES WS-MSG-NO PIC X(04) (:46-:47) the four-character string '2513' at offset 15: a '513', a ' 513', an '02513' or a JSON number would silently break the tolerance branch at all four call sites. This case reaches arm 5 by a second and independent route. case10 reaches it with '1582-10-14', the eve of the Lillian epoch and one of the ten days the Gregorian reform skipped, so by a below-epoch calendar date; this case reaches it with a SUPPORTED era name that places the date before the common era, which precedes that epoch by construction. The two therefore agree byte for byte on the severity '0003', on the message number '2513' and on the result text 'Unsupp. Range  ', and differ only in the two spans their differing LINKAGE pairs feed - the echoed date at offsets 45-54 and the mask at offsets 66-75 - so an implementation that guarded only one end of the range, or only the calendar route into it, would fail exactly one of the pair. Read beside case09, which passes the unsupported era name 'XX' and lands on 2509 instead, it also proves the era field is genuinely decoded rather than skipped: 'BC' is accepted as a name and then rejected on range, where 'XX' is rejected as a name. The echoed date is CORRUPT BY DESIGN and the corruption is preserved rather than corrected. :105 moves LENGTH OF LS-DATE - the declared PIC X(10) width, so always 10 - into VSTRING-LENGTH, giving the halfword 0x000A; :107-:108 puts the date into WS-DATE; :116 calls CEEDAYS; then :122 MOVE WS-DATE-TO-TEST TO WS-DATE is a GROUP move whose source begins with Vstring-length PIC S9(4) BINARY, so the receiving WS-DATE PIC X(10) takes the leftmost ten bytes - the two binary length bytes 0x00 and 0x0A followed by only the first eight characters, 'BC220719', the two trailing blanks of the parameter falling off the end - and :122 therefore overwrites what :107 had written. WS-DATE-FMT at offsets 66-75 is clean by contrast, because :111-:113 sets it before the call and :122 targets WS-DATE alone. The eighty bytes are 4 + 11 + 4 + 1 + 15 + 1 + 9 + 10 + 1 + 10 + 10 + 1 + 3, summed mechanically from the 01 WS-MESSAGE declaration at :42-:57, where two of the three literal FILLERs are shorter than the span holding them - 'Mesg Code:' is 10 characters in a PIC X(11) and 'TstDate:' is 8 in a PIC X(09), both right space-padded by their VALUE clause - while 'Mask used:' is exactly 10 in a PIC X(10) and needs no pad, which is precisely what makes the other two easy to overlook. INITIALIZE WS-MESSAGE at :90 does not clear a FILLER, so all three literals always appear. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of that declaration and of the group move at :122; they are NOT captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL, which is empirically impossible in this environment because no Language Environment service is reachable - a search of the available compiler's intrinsics matches zero CEE* entries, so the CALL "CEEDAYS" at :116 that decides every one of these outcomes has no implementation to call. That substitution changes only the provenance of the expected values, leaving the twenty cases, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-of-zero gate all standing, and it is recorded as the highest-severity open risk in the Agent Action Plan rather than silently absorbed. review_rules reports no user rules provided for this project, so no user rule governs this fixture and none has been invented; the enterprise practices the plan substitutes apply instead, which is why the two non-printable bytes are written as explicit escapes under US-ASCII rather than as raw control characters, why every trailing space is written out rather than left to a pad, and why the reference COBOL this case is derived from was read and never modified.

THE TWO CALL PARAMETERS, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. unitStimulus.linkage carries this case's whole input: LS-DATE = 'BC220719  ' and LS-DATE-FORMAT = '<BC>YYMMDD', each written out to the ten characters PIC X(10) declares at app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl:84-85 with every trailing space visible - a mask longer than ten characters is TRUNCATED by the receiving field, and the truncation changes the message number, so the width has to be readable at the point the value is written. CSUTLDTC seeds no dataset and drives no screen, so these two values are the only thing a case varies; they used to live in a table in CSUTLDTCParityTest keyed by 'case01'..'case20', which meant this file stated an eighty-byte result with nothing in it to say what was validated, and cases that differ only in their input were indistinguishable on disk.
